## 1. Load the processed data

```{r load packages and data}

library(psych)

H1 <- read.csv("Data/Processed_Data/h1.csv")
H2 <- read.csv("Data/Processed_Data/h2.csv")



```


```{r variable distributions}

#H1:

hist(H1$path_sum,
     main = "Distribution of History of Infection",
     xlab = "Composite Pathogen Score (0-18)")

sum(H1$Sex_birth == "Intersex") #49
sum(H1$Sex_birth == "Male") #4004
sum(H1$Sex_birth == "Female") #5019


#H2: 

hist(H2$pol_diff,
     main = "Distribution of Political Difference in Relationships",
     xlab = "Political Difference (0-4)")

hist(H2$prqc_3,
     main = "Distribution of Happiness in Relationship",
     xlab = "Relatinship Happiness (1-7)")


```


```{r individual statistics}

#H1

mean(H1$path_sum, na.rm = TRUE) #2.15388
median(H1$path_sum, na.rm = TRUE) #1
IQR(H1$path_sum, na.rm = TRUE) #1

table(H1$Sex_birth, useNA = "ifany")

#Female Intersex     Male 
#  5019       49     4004 


#H2

mean(H2$prqc_3, na.rm = TRUE) #5.484982
median(H2$prqc_3, na.rm = TRUE) #6
IQR(H2$prqc_3, na.rm = TRUE) #2

mean(H2$pol_diff, na.rm = TRUE) #1.294322
median(H2$pol_diff, na.rm = TRUE) #1
IQR(H2$pol_diff, na.rm = TRUE) #1



```


```{r standardize variables}

#H1:

H1$path_z <- scale(H1$path_sum)

mean(H1$path_z, na.rm = TRUE) #Almost zero 
sd(H1$path_z, na.rm = TRUE) #1




#H2: 

H2$happiness_z <- scale(H2$prqc_3)

# Standardized scores have mean approximately 0 and standard deviation 1.
mean(H2$happiness_z, na.rm = TRUE) #Almost zero 
sd(H2$happiness_z, na.rm = TRUE) #1


H2$pol_diff_z <- scale(H2$pol_diff)

mean(H2$pol_diff_z, na.rm = TRUE) #Almost zero 
sd(H2$pol_diff_z, na.rm = TRUE) #1



```


```{r Covariance for H2}
# Covariance describes whether two variables tend to move together.
# Positive: higher values tend to occur together. Negative: higher values tend to accompany lower values.
# Its size depends on the units and is not restricted to -1 through 1.
#use = complete.obs means you only use if there's observations for both

cov(H2$pol_diff, H2$prqc_3, use = "complete.obs") # -0.06488937

# Pearson correlation expresses a linear association on a -1 to 1 scale.
cor(H2$pol_diff, H2$prqc_3, use = "complete.obs") # -0.07551288
#slight negative correlation

# Make a correlation table: Select numerical variables only; do not include participant IDs or category codes.
corData <- H2[,c("pol_diff", "prqc_3")]
cor(corData, use = "complete.obs")

```


```{r combined summaries}
# summary() reports minimum, quartiles, median, mean, maximum, and missing counts when present.
summary(corData)

# psych::describe() reports n, mean, SD, median, minimum, maximum, range width (max minus min), skewness, kurtosis, and other summaries.
describe(corData)

```
